preamble: Insertion of [f] is rare. Its best-known source is the Goidelic languages, where initial lenition deletes f (written fh and silent). Since lenited f-words look vowel-initial, speakers reanalysed some genuinely vowel-initial words as lenited f-words and restored an f that had never been there, as in Old Irish úar 'cold' > Irish fuar and Old Irish ásaid 'grows' > Irish and Scottish Gaelic fás / fàs. This is an analogical prothesis driven by the mutation system, not a phonetic transition sound.

examples.note: The f arose because uar was misinterpreted as lenited fhuar.

examples.from: Old Irish ásaid, verbal noun áss 'growing'
examples.note: ás- was reinterpreted as fhás- in lenition environments.
Middle Irish already shows both íarfaigid and fíarfaigid.
Ulster Irish uiseog and Scottish Gaelic uiseag keep the f-less form.
